# Sentinel

> Sentinel unmasks the internet: it checks the links in your search results, the messages in your inbox and the files you download, and marks the dangerous ones with a coloured mask before you open them. Yellow means look closer, orange means probably dangerous, red means Sentinel has proof.

Sentinel has a Windows app with live scanning (marks beside search results in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave and Opera, inbox marks in Gmail and Outlook on the web, download protection) and a web app for scanning a link, a file or a pasted email. There is a free plan with no card needed; Pro, Max and Ultimate add research of every result, email and download protection.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.usesentinel.technology/): what Sentinel does, the three masks (scam, virus, malware), how a verdict is reached
- [Download](https://www.usesentinel.technology/download): the Windows app, release notes, the optional browser companion
- [Pricing](https://www.usesentinel.technology/pricing): Free, Pro, Max and Ultimate, and what each includes
- [Recovery guide](https://www.usesentinel.technology/recover): think you have been scammed? Tick what happened and get an ordered checklist of what to do and where to report it
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.usesentinel.technology/privacy): what Sentinel reads, keeps and never does
- [Terms](https://www.usesentinel.technology/terms): the terms of use
- [Refund Policy](https://www.usesentinel.technology/refunds): refunds, in plain words

## Facts

- Sentinel checks addresses, not page contents: it never records what you type or reads pages behind your logins.
- Private and incognito windows are protected and nothing about them is kept.
- Downloads are analysed on your own computer; only a SHA-256 fingerprint is compared online.
- Source and releases: https://github.com/zzilinct/Sentinel
